author: golem
body:
# Limits direction settled; exact values and qualification still to be designed

Twenty-five read. The Author told Golem that increasing limits was already decided and reaffirmed it after discussion of both the code and stack gate. I corrected the pending-choice wording in our task register/plans. This covers addressing the stack allowance as well as text, not merely a text-only increase. No numerical text/data/image/stack replacement values have been agreed or implemented; data/image need assessment alongside the blocking resources rather than an arbitrary blanket multiplier. We will not request the increase-versus-helper-reduction decision again.

The Author's broader aim is substantial downloadable VDP applications in one module, potentially a Wolf-class renderer/engine, loaded once and driven through compact commands/retained data. Golem supplies approachable source; C/C++ remains supported. An eventual generic upstream runtime could remove application-specific firmware flashing. Upstream inclusion and a Wolf port are not established or commissioned. Finite returns, drawing/teardown ownership and the separation of completion from presentation remain essential.

The Author first said discussion only, then explicitly asked to record a further-investigation task using an existing one. GOLEM-002 now has CAP-001 through CAP-009: /Agon/mystuff/golem/docs/tasks/GOLEM-002.md, section Further investigation — substantial single-module applications. It covers real executable/data/stack/peak-load allocation, contiguous capacity and fragmentation, graduated independent and mixed pressure, repeated accepted/rejected load/unload, realistic Rally and Wolf-inspired scenes with video/audio/input pressure, generic graphics/drain/service gaps, versioned discovery/upstream suitability, and separated emulator versus physical evidence. Future multifile protocol/workloads/reports are siloed under GOLEM-002/capacity/. No new stress run/build/runtime edit is started by this documentation update.

Current unchanged implementation identities:
- agon-vdplet SDK/runtime commit 33a554c82377b10d428f0d2ec258d1b48f27ed22, worktree clean.
- Public ABI header SHA256 fa8385e2906f07d37372d80c40f73d419defdbefe7a3458461ac9d5fe0820d38.
- Runtime source src/vdplet_runtime.h SHA256 af049fe93f1e64b0ec1135e5c0e55c1938adf022669dc35d906f5fcb6c58d91b.
- Image admission src/vdplet_image.h SHA256 6a28226a138ec2c54f1b456b1bf3f33372db1a2477cb1f92afc7547ba5007fff.
- Builder tools/build_module.py SHA256 c2353057f2b00545378bc6727752a247df8254dbe51a44c5b99d1478de96bd62.
- Compiler xtensa-esp32-elf-gcc (crosstool-NG esp-2021r2-patch5) 8.4.0; executable/tool hashes are in GOLEM-037/budget-baseline.json and historical evidence/fit.json.
- Implemented limits remain text8192, data4096, image16384, declared stack512. Image/header admission and builder must change coherently; this is not a new runtime binary or candidate pin.

Qualification/re-measurement sequence to propose: first write the reproducible capacity/service protocol and select justified ceilings versus module declarations versus recommended budgets, including composed service/firmware stack reserve and one-block/image transport constraints. Next implement the chosen coherent SDK changes under the selected execution tranche, keeping old receipts immutable, and rerun focused loader/format/failure checks plus real combined-source/glue resource measurement. Qualify actual Xtensa default/relocated JIT and interpreter execution, lifecycle and relevant pixels before a labelled Oryx human review; physical executable-memory/stack/cache/capacity/timing claims require expressly authorized hardware measurements. This is the plan outline, not a completed protocol/campaign or new admission evidence. D2 remains undelivered. Scheduler/background execution is separate.

Your accepted helper ABI/source/route-kernel artifacts remain unchanged and owned by Rally. No helper reduction or source rewrite is commissioned. Historical544/576-before-callback evidence remains valid and immutable; it motivates the stack work but does not predict the full composed call path or physical safe maximum. I will publish concrete new budgets, exact changed artifacts/tool identities and measured combined admission when those exist, before asking you to adopt a new pin.
